Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 40,00,000/- from the date of accident till its realization for the fatal injury sustained by Smt. Reena Devi, aged about 30 years in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 03.11.2019 at about 1:15 AM, near 42-7 km, Lucknow Expressway, MACP No. 224/20; FIR No.
267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 involving Bus bearing registration no. UP22T-3823 (offending vehicle)
which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 03.11.2019, deceased Smt. Reena Devi and her husband Sh. Matashran were coming to Delhi from Madhogarh by aforesaid bus bearing registration no. UP22T-3823 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high, in a rash and negligent manner and in a zigzag manner.

At about 1:15 AM, when the bus reached near 42-7 km, Lucknow Expressway, driver of the aforesaid bus lost his control and hit the same against a truck from its back side with a great force, as a result of which Smt. Reena Devi and other passengers sustained grievous injuries.

She was immediately taken to CHC Hospital,
Sikohabad, Firozabad and thereafter, she was referred to District Hospital Saifai, where doctor declared her 'brought dead' and her postmortem was conduced at District Mortuary, Safai, UP.
A case U/s 279/338/304A IPC was registered at PS. Matsena, vide FIR No. 267/19 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3/New India Assurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.

5. From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order dated 23.03.2021:-
1) Whether the deceased Ms. Reena Devi suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 03.11.2019 at about 1:15 AM near 42-7 km, Lucknow Expressway within the jurisdiction of PS Matsena, District Firozabad, due to rashness and negligence on the part of driver Sh. Pardeep Kumar/R-1 who was driving the vehicle bearing registration no. UP22T-3823, owned by Sh. Raghav/R-2 and insured with the New India Assurance Company Limited/R-3?OPP.
2) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP.

267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 the accident) as PW-1 and PW-2 Sh. Brajesh Chandra,
Pharmacist, from the office of Joint Hospital, Shikohabad, UP and closed their evidence on 03.12.2024.

On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and RE of insurance company was closed vide order dated 03.12.2024.

sentences.text: However, during the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners has shown the original voter I Card of deceased and the same was returned after seeing the same, the copy of which is already marked as Mark Y. PW1 in his testimony by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A)

has deposed that on 03.11.2019, he alongwith his wife Smt. Reena Devi were coming to Delhi from Madhogarh by offending bus bearing registration no. UP22T-3823 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high, in a rash and negligent manner and in a zigzag manner.

He further deposed that at about 1:15 AM, when they reached near 42-7 km, Lucknow Expressway, driver of the aforesaid bus lost his control and hit the same against a truck from its back side with a great force, as a result of which his wife Smt. Reena Devi and other passengers sustained grievous injuries.

He further deposed that deceased was immediately taken to CHC Hospital, Sikohabad, Firozabad and thereafter, she was referred to District Hospital Saifai, where doctor declared her 'brought dead' and her postmortem was conduced at District Mortuary, Safai, UP.
During his cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company
, he deposed that he had not filed on record any bus ticket.
He denied the suggestion that he was not travelling in a bus bearing no. UP22T-3823.
He further denied the suggestion that the driver of aforesaid bus was not negligent at the time of accident.

It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the insurance company could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Moreover, FIR No. 267/19 is shown to have been registered on the statement of this witness i.e. PW1 Sh. Matashran.
The contents of said FIR would show that he had disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident, as deposed by him as PW1 during the course of inquiry.

Moreover, the respondent has not led any evidence to rebut the testimony of aforesaid witness on the aspect of accident in question being caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the uncontroverted testimony of this witness made on oath.

11. It is the contention of Ld. Counsel for insurance company that since the husband of deceased had failed to produce the bus ticket, therefore, it can not be said that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehcile.

It is seen that testimony of PW2 shows that deceased was admitted in serious condition in the hospital on the date of accident alongwith 23 other patients who were also travelling in the offending vehicle.

Hence, there is no merit contention raised by the counsel for Matashran And Ors vs Pradeep Kumar on 1 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137136955/

sentences.text:
There is no merit in the contention raised on behalf of insurance company that testimony of PW1 is liable to be discarded on the ground that FIR in the present case was registered on 11.11.2019 i.e.
after delay of about 8 days from the date of accident.
No doubt, accident occurred on 03.11.2019 and FIR in the present case, was registered on 11.11.2019 i.e. after about 8 days from the date of accident.

The complainant/PW1 who was also travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident and on whose statement FIR in the present matter was registered has explained in his statement that his wife who is deceased in the present matter suffered sustained serious injuries in the accident and he specifically mentioned the registration number of offending vehicle in his statement.
Even otherwise, no question was put by the insurance company during cross-examination of PW1 as regards the explanation for delay in registration of FIR.
13. Be that as it may, GD No. 022 was recorded in PS. Madhaugarh, on the basis of a call received from caller on 04.11.2019 at 12:11(accident being caused on 03.11.2019 at 1:15 AM).

Thus, it follows from the aforesaid discussion that the accident in question had taken place while respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle at a very high speed and he could not keep control over the offending vehicle and ultimately, hit against the other vehicle i.e., truck.

The facts and circumstances as brought on record, would show that said vehicle was being driven at very high speed due to which MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 respondent no. 1 could not manage to stop the vehicle, which resulted into the accident in question.

Not only this, the circumstances showing that accident resulted into fatal injuries to deceased and injuries to other passengers who were travelling in the offending vehicle is also relevant to infer the impact of the accident and the manner in which it would have taken place.

14. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same can not be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.

Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
While saying so, I am also fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter titled as "Ravi Vs. Badri Narayan & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on 18.02.2011.

sentences.text: Hence, I am of the view that the delay of about 8 days in registration of FIR in this case has been sufficiently explained and the claimants can not be denied just and fair compensation on this ground.

15. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.

17. A bare perusal of document Ex. PW2/2 which is Out Patient Department Register, District Joint Hospital, Firozabad shows that deceased Reena was admitted in the said hospital on 04.11.2019 at 2:00 AM with alleged history of RTA alongwith other injured persons.
These documents have not been disputed from the side of insurance company.
18. Postmortem was also got conducted on the body of deceased Smt. Reena Devi.
The copy of PM Report of deceased, would show that cause of death of deceased has been opined due to shock and hemorrhage and antemortem head injury.
The external injuries as mentioned in the relevant column correspond with the injuries which occur in Motor Vehicular Accident.
These documents have not been disputed from the side of insurance company.

19. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderence of probabilities that Smt. Reena Devi had sustained fatal injuries in the road accident which took place on 03.11.2019 at about 1:15 AM, near 42-7 km, Lucknow Expressway, due to rash and negligent MACP No. 224/20; FIR No.
267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 driving on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Thus, this issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
20. The petitioners who are claimants are the husband and two minor daughters of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

21. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -

sentences.text: "The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation &
Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation &
Anr.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
22. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

In case titled Kirti & Anr. Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166, 3-Judge Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court while discussing and highlighting the services rendered by housewife/homemaker and assessment of her notional income as per minimum wages prescribed for the State observed as under:
xxxxx " Grant of compensation, on a pecuniary basis, with respect to a homemaker, is a settled proposition of law.

entities.text: Kirti & Anr. Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Taking into account the gendered nature of housework,
with an overwhelming percentage of women being engaged in the same as compared to men, the fixing of notional income of a homemaker attains special significance.
It becomes a recognition of the work, labour and sacrifices of homemakers and a reflection of changing attitudes.
It is also in furtherance of our nation's international law obligations and our constitutional vision of social equality and ensuring dignity to all.
Various methods can be employed by the Court to fix the notional income of a homemaker, depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.

The Court should ensure while choosing the method, and fixing the notional income, that the same is just in the facts and circumstances of the particular case, neither assessing the compensation too conservatively, nor too liberally.

The granting of future prospects,on the MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 notional income calculated in such cases, is a component of just compensation"
xxxxx 27.

In the matter titled as Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited Vs. Manmeet Singh & Ors.", reported at 2012 ACJ 721 (Delhi), it has been held by Hon'ble Delhi High Court that the services rendered by a housewife can not be counted; cooking, washing, ironing clothes and stitching clothes (in some cases) for the husband and children, teaching and guiding children,
working as a nurse whenever the husband and child/children are sick, are some of the major activities of a housewife.

Though, PW-1 has stated in his evidence that deceased was working as Labour and was earning Rs. 18,000/-per month at the time of accident, however, he has also admitted in his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company that he had not filed any documentary proof in respect of working and earning of deceased at the time of accident.

It is also relevant to note here that while deciding claim petition under M.V Act, it is the duty of Claims Tribunal to follow the principles of justice, equity and good MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 conscience and to adopt more realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am of the considered view that loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of a skilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question.

31. PW1 Sh. Matashran has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A)
that all the petitioners were dependent upon the deceased at the time of accident.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company argued that husband of deceased was not dependent upon the deceased at the time of accident and there were only two dependants upon the deceased who are minor children of deceased.
It is relevant to mention here that said part of his testimony remained unchallanged.

After considering the entire facts as apparent on record and the fact that the petitioner no. 1/husband of deceased was also definitely dependent upon his wife/deceased for her household services and other services.

In view of the same, it is held that there were three dependents upon the deceased i.e.
husband and two minor children of deceased at the time of accident and there has to be deduction of one third as held in the case of Sarla Verma mentioned supra.
Thus, the total loss of dependency would come out to Rs. 32,23,987.20p (Rs. 17,991/- X 2/3 X 140/100 X 12 X 16).

Hence, a sum of Rs.
32,23,987.20p is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is seen that testimony of PW2 shows that deceased was admitted in serious condition in the hospital on the date of accident alongwith 23 other patients who were also travelling in the offending vehicle.
No doubt, accident occurred on 03.11.2019 and FIR in the present case, was registered on 11.11.2019 i.e. after about 8 days from the date of accident.
The facts and circumstances as brought on record, would show that said vehicle was being driven at very high speed due to which MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 respondent no. 1 could not manage to stop the vehicle, which resulted into the accident in question.
Not only this, the circumstances showing that accident resulted into fatal injuries to deceased and injuries to other passengers who were travelling in the offending vehicle is also relevant to infer the impact of the accident and the manner in which it would have taken place.
14. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same can not be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.
Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
Hence, I am of the view that the delay of about 8 days in registration of FIR in this case has been sufficiently explained and the claimants can not be denied just and fair compensation on this ground.
15. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how MACP No. 224/20; FIR No. 267/19 DOD:01.05.2025 and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.

V. Kamlesh & Ors, MAC APP. No. 530/2008 passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court on 11.11.2008.
